_about: Provisional labels, judged by a model (Fable) from tile renders of the flattened stack, not by the owner: a proxy to optimise towards until corrected models exist. curves: a traced edge with verdict "vessel", "not" or "unsure", as points in µm from the image's top-left. missed: vessels the judge saw with no trace, as rough polylines in µm. box_um: the judged tile; outside it nothing is labelled.

tiles.notes: Hard calls were the faint short traces east of the loop: 6 partly follows a faint streak beyond the bright blob but then hooks through speckle; 22 and 23 sit entirely on granular speckle with no continuous line beneath. The bright vessel stub entering at the top edge near x=128 has no trace.

The faint horizontal vessel along y~115 is traced in three disconnected pieces (12/11, 10, 39) leaving an untraced stretch around x 50-74; most other short cyan curves (loops 17/18, 32/35/36 and the clusters at 20-25, 26/28, 31/33/34) sit on granular speckle with no followable line in the bare image. The bright elongated blob at (145,55) is probably a vessel fragment but is hard to call from a max projection.

The junction cluster at (115-125, 112-122) is split into many tiny stubs (13,15,16,41,42,43) that are hard to judge individually; the faint wavy traces 35 and 50 sit near low-contrast grey that might be out-of-focus vessel but look like speckle-following.

The bright irregular mass across y 100-150 is hard to parse into individual vessels, so traces 26-31 and the small loop 36-39 inside it are judged on plausibility rather than clear lines; no curve numbered 7 is visible in the panel. Faint dim capillaries in the lower right were missed entirely while speckle arcs (33, 35) were traced.

Hard parts: the faint capillaries in the dark lower-left and upper-right quadrants (36/38/45/47/49/50/52/53/57, 19/10/14) sit at speckle brightness so most are 'unsure'; several traces (29, 55/66, 54/67) duplicate or cut across the thick vessels, and 24/62/63/25/64 are wiggly speckle walks. Curves 3 and 5 are not visible on the panel.
